lines.trans: Vika, my dear, please forgive me!
I made a terrible mistake, I am guilty.
I love you very much!
Let us start everything from the very beginning.
Pasha, where is my money?
What money? What are you talking about?
The money that you stole from the nightstand.
I did not take anything from your nightstand!
Only you knew about this hiding place.
Where did you put them, answer me!
Vikusya, calm down, let us talk calmly.
Do not touch me until you return the money!

meanings.note: Habitually or in general. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to take', paired with 'взять'.
'брать' alone often means this, in talk about officials

examples.trans: We have to take all the money.

вернуть.gloss: to give back, to get back

meanings.note: + accusative. Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to give back, to get back', paired with 'возвращать'.
Money you spent. Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to give back, to get back', paired with 'возвращать'.

examples.text: Ты эти деньги через полгода вернёшь.
examples.trans: You'll get this money back in six months.

meanings.note: The neuter form 'всё' used alone. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.
Neuter всё. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.
Plural все. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.
short forms виноват / виновата / виноваты are used for 'it's my/your fault'

examples.text: Я ни в чём не виноват.
examples.trans: I'm not to blame for anything.

meanings.note: Location; for direction use 'куда'. Core Russian adv meaning 'where' in everyday speech.

examples.text: А где машинка? Где моя машинка?
examples.trans: Hey, where's the toy car? Where's my toy car?

meanings.note: Что за глупости? = What nonsense?. Abstract feminine noun formed with the Slavic suffix '-ость' ('-ness, -ity') from the corresponding adjective. Common feminine noun meaning 'nonsense, foolishness' in everyday Russian.
Abstract feminine noun formed with the Slavic suffix '-ость' ('-ness, -ity') from the corresponding adjective. Common feminine noun meaning 'nonsense, foolishness' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Что за глупости? Значит, Осипенко сам эти деньги украл!
examples.trans: What nonsense? That means Osipenko stole that money himself!

говорить.gloss: to speak, to say, to talk

meanings.note: Я тебе говорю = I'm telling you. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to speak, to say, to talk', paired with 'сказать'.
Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to speak, to say, to talk', paired with 'сказать'.
давай + 1st person plural or infinitive
давай + 1st person plural or infinitive

examples.text: Давай мы его уволим, а тебя на его место назначим.
examples.trans: Let's fire him and put you in his place.

meanings.note: plural only: there is no singular in everyday use

examples.trans: The money is on the table.
Gum? I didn't have enough money.

meanings.en: to put, do with, dispose of (colloquial)
meanings.note: Куда ты дел...? = Where did you put / What did you do with...?

examples.text: Куда ты дел их деньги на новое здание?
examples.trans: Where did you put their money for the new building?
Where did I put the keys?

examples.text: Да? А спросите у него, куда он дел компьютерный класс.
examples.trans: Really? Then ask him where he put the computer lab.

meanings.note: to a loved one, and at the start of letters
to a loved one, and at the start of letters

examples.text: В Москве вам дают деньги на дорогую одежду, а мозги не дают.
examples.trans: In Moscow they give you money for expensive clothes, but they don't give you brains.

meanings.note: A fact or a person. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to know'.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: + genitive: 'из мэрии' = from the town hall

examples.text: Марина Сергеевна, я уже знаю. Мне звонили из мэрии.
examples.trans: Marina Sergeyevna, I already know. The town hall called me.

meanings.note: In questions. Core Russian det meaning 'what; what a' in everyday speech.
in exclamations: какой грязный! = how dirty!

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: joins a description to a noun; agrees with that noun in gender and number

examples.trans: This is a mayor who keeps his word.
Where is the book that was here?

examples.text: А что я за мэр такой, который держит своё слово?
examples.trans: And what kind of mayor would I be if I kept my word?

meanings.note: For movement; где is for location. Core Russian adv meaning 'where (to)' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Wait, where are you two going?

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to love, to like', paired with 'полюбить'.
Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to love, to like', paired with 'полюбить'.

examples.trans: I love our town very much.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Agrees with the thing owned. Core Russian det meaning 'my, mine' in everyday speech.
Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'чало'). Common neuter noun meaning 'beginning' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: At the beginning of the week.

examples.text: Ваня, это теперь твоё. И это только начало.
examples.trans: Vanya, this is yours now. And it's only the beginning.

meanings.note: + imperfective infinitive or + accusative

examples.text: Это хорошо, что готово. А то мы уже начали беспокоиться.
examples.trans: It's good that it's ready. We were starting to worry.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates
usually in the genitive ничего, with не: ничего не осталось

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: + prepositional; об before a vowel: об этом

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.
examples.trans: I have no time to think about that. There's too much to do.

meanings.note: Core Russian pron meaning 'they' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Ты преподавай. А они пусть строят свои торговые центры.
examples.trans: You teach. And let them build their shopping centres.

meanings.en: to answer, to reply, to pick up the phone
meanings.note: Отвечать кому / на звонок. Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'вечать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to answer, to reply', paired with 'ответить'.

examples.text: Я вам звоню, а вы не отвечаете!
examples.trans: I call you, and you don't answer!

examples.text: Почему ты не отвечаешь на мои вопросы?
examples.trans: Why aren't you answering my questions?

meanings.note: With verbs: очень люблю. Core Russian adv meaning 'very, very much' in everyday speech.
With verbs: очень люблю. Core Russian adv meaning 'very, very much' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: I love our town very much.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.en: to have a talk, to speak (with someone)
meanings.note: Поговорить с + instrumental. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'говорить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to have a talk', paired with 'говорить'.

examples.text: Поговори с Аракеляном. Пусть он заберёт заявление.
examples.trans: Talk to Arakelyan. Get him to withdraw his statement.

meanings.note: Handing something over. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'жалуйста').
Answer to thanks. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'жалуйста').
Handing something over. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'жалуйста').
А пока = but for now. Core Russian adv meaning 'for now, meanwhile; while; bye' in everyday speech.
As a conjunction: пока я сплю. Core Russian adv meaning 'for now, meanwhile; while; bye' in everyday speech.
Informal goodbye. Core Russian adv meaning 'for now, meanwhile; while; bye' in everyday speech.

Простите! = sorry! forgive me!. Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'стить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to forgive; (imperative) excuse me', paired with 'прощать'.

Imperative: прости / простите. Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'стить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to forgive; (imperative) excuse me', paired with 'прощать'.
+ instrumental; со before some consonant clusters: со всеми

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: forms the superlative: самый главный = the most important
Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'амый'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('the most; the very').

examples.trans: The most important thing is the people.
Do you know the main thing?

meanings.note: Adverb of degree. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ильно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: The wind is blowing hard outside.

examples.text: Я так два года потеряла. Любила так сильно!
examples.trans: I lost two years like that. I loved him so much!

meanings.note: a formal, bookish verb; used jokingly about everyday things
совершить ошибку = to make a mistake

examples.trans: Daddy's already had his cold dip.
Rise and shine! Daddy's already had his cold dip.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'покойно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Его не будет часа два. Вы спокойно всё сделаете.
examples.trans: He'll be gone for about two hours. You'll do everything calmly.

meanings.note: Secret storage spot. Derived noun with agent/object suffix '-ник'/'-щик'/'-чик'. Common masculine noun meaning 'hiding place, secret stash' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Only you knew about this hiding place.

examples.text: Как? Ты?! А как же адвокатская тайна?
examples.trans: How? You?! What about lawyer-client secrecy?

meanings.note: To someone you call ты. Core Russian det meaning 'your (informal)' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Я бы на твоём месте подумал.
examples.trans: If I were you, I'd think about it.

meanings.note: softens a request: только не сердись = just don't be angry
Не трогай! = Don't touch!. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to touch', paired with 'тронуть'.

examples.text: Всё, хорошо, я тебя выпущу! Только собаку не трогай!
examples.trans: All right, fine, I'll let you out! Just don't touch the dog!

meanings.note: Small bedroom cabinet. Formed with a diminutive/expressive Slavic suffix adding warmth or small scale. Common feminine noun meaning 'nightstand, bedside table' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Деньги, которые ты украл из тумбочки.
examples.trans: The money that you stole from the nightstand.

examples.text: Я ничего не брал из твоей тумбочки!
examples.trans: I did not take anything from your nightstand!

meanings.note: One person, informal. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (informal)' in everyday speech.

meanings.en: other forms: тебя (gen/acc), тебе (dat), тобой (instr), тебе (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (informal)' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'жасный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('horrible, terrible').

examples.trans: What a horrible person you are!

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'красть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to steal', paired with 'красть'.

examples.text: Чтобы он вернул деньги, которые украл.
examples.trans: For him to give back the money he stole.

meanings.en: to calm down, to settle down
meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'спокоиться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to calm down', paired with 'успокаиваться'.
Question word. Core Russian pron meaning 'what' in everyday speech.
Conjunction. Core Russian pron meaning 'what' in everyday speech.
Core Russian pron meaning 'what' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: alone: 'я этого не хочу' = I don't want that

examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat.

examples.text: Меня уже тошнит от этой коммуналки! У нас труба уже неделю течёт.
examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat! Our pipe has been leaking for a week now.

meanings.note: меня = me (genitive/accusative), мне = to me (dative)

meanings.en: other forms: меня (gen/acc), мне (dat), мной (instr), мне (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'I' in everyday speech.
+ genitive. Core Russian prep meaning 'until, before; up to' in everyday speech.
Core Russian prep meaning 'until, before; up to' in everyday speech.

related.gloss: to reach, walk as far as

meanings.note: Literally 'until the meeting'. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'видание'). Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'meeting; date' in everyday Russian.

Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'видание'). Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'meeting; date' in everyday Russian.
